THE COMPANY CAME OUT TO TIGHTEN THE VALVE BUT NEVER CLEANED UP THE SPILLED OIL. THE CALLER STATES THAT HE PULLED UP THE CARPET BUT THE SMELL IS CAUSING ISSUES FOR HIS FAMILY. THE CALLER IS WAITING ON AN INSURANCE CLAIM TO BE ISSUED BUT IS CONCERNED WITH THE FUMES THEY HAVE BEEN BREATHING SINCE AUG 9, 2017. THERE IS ALSO CARPET SOAKED IN OIL UNDER THE FURNACE.

REPORT DETAILS: FROM WINDSOR ONTARIO REPORTING DOCK SLUMP AT WINDSOR PORT OF WINDSOR 120 BROADWAY STREET, WINDSOR. SOLID SUSPENSION IN WATER - GRANULAR DUST IN THE PILE THAT HAD COLLAPSED. DOCK USED AS AN AGGREGATE DOCK (CRUSH STONE). EST 12,000 METRIC TONS OF MATERIAL INVOLVED - PILE WENT STRAIGHT DOWN AND PUSHED SHORELINE OUT AND COLLAPSED THE SHORE LINE - PILE WENT DOWN 25 FEET AND THAT PUSHED BARRIER SHORELINE OUT INTO THE RIVER AND IT APPEARS TO HAVE RAISED BOTTOM OF THE DETROIT RIVER. SHORELINE 55 METERS AFFECTED. INCIDENT TOOK PLACE 1750. OWNER OF THE FACILITY (BRIDGEPORT AGGREGATES OWNED BY SOUTHWEST SALES). CALLER NOTES HE JUST LEFT SITE - NOTHING APPEARS TO BE MOVING - SUSPENDED FINES ARE FLOATING DOWN THE RIVER - SORT OF ON THE SURFACE AS DUST, DIFFUSE LOOKING LIKE LITTLE FOAM PACKETS FLOATING DOWN THE RIVER. CALLER ESTIMATES 55 METERS BY 10 METERS RIVER AREA AFFECTED.

properties.title: NRC Report: Oil, Fuel: No. 1-D in Pacific Ocean
properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 820764 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party:
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 820764
Incident Time: 2006-11-29 13:00:00
Nearest City: HI
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 1-D
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 3.25 gallons
WEB REPORT/////////INCIDENT DESCRIPTION: 11/29/2006 - 11/30/2006 OBSERVED HYDRAULIC OIL LEAKING ONTO THE DECK. UNDER FURTHER EXAMINATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS A LINE LEAK. WHEN THE SYSTEM REACHED A POINT WHERE THE REEL WOULD NO LONGER OPERATE, THE CAPTAIN STOPPED FISHING OPERATIONS, AND ATTEMPTED TO FIX THE PROBLEM. BY 00:19, I WAS FILMING THE LEAK WHILE THE CREW REPAIRED THE LINE. AT APPROXIMATELY 02:30, I OBSERVED A CREWMAN DUMP 2 TO 3 GALLONS OF OIL COLLECTED DIRECTLY OVER THE STARBOARD BEAM. POSITION 23 46.1N 156 55.8W. I SAID NO, NO, NO TO THE CREW AS HE DUMPED IT, THE CAPTAIN WAS NOT PRESENT.12/1/2006 AT APPROXIMATELY 10:30, BECAME AWARE THAT THE BILGE HAD BEEN PUMPED. I HAD OBSERVED OVER THE PREVIOUS DAYS A RELATIVE LACK OF WATER ACCUMULATING IN THE BILGE, AT TRIPS BEGINNING, THE HULL WAS CLEARLY VISIBLE, WITH THE PASSING DAYS, THE LEVEL OF LEAKED OIL HAD INCREASED WELL ABOVE THE LONGITUDINAL PROFILES AND STRINGERS. ON THE MORNING OF THE 1ST OF DECEMBER 2006 IT WAS CLEAR THAT WHILE I SLEPT, THE BILGE HAD BEEN PUMPED. 12/6/2006 AT 10:26, I AWOKE TO THE BOAT'S LACK OF FORWARD MOTION AND SILENCED MAIN ENGINE, I CLIMBED DOWN TO THE ENGINE ROOM TO INVESTIGATE, THERE I OBSERVED CAPTAIN MUOI CLEANING A DIESEL FILTER FOR THE MAIN ENGINE, AND DUMPING THE DYED DIESEL THAT WAS BEING USED TO BREAK UP THE SLUDGE, DIRECTLY INTO THE BILGE. I RETURNED TO MY BUNK TO RECORD THE EVENT AFTER CHECKING THE LAT/LON, 22 37.21N 158 01.9 W. THESE ISSUES WERE NOT POINTED OUT TO THE CAPTAIN.
